3.1 **Pedestrian Bridge Lighting – Jalan Besar** (M-2022-14)

3.2 **Community Centre Air-Conditioning Upgrade** (M-2022-17)
The upgrade is progessing well. The contractor has advised a minor delay due to parts availability. Revised completion date is 20 February 2023. A progress report will be tabled at the February meeting.

3.3 **Audit of 2021 Annual Report – Follow-up**
Internal Audit reported that 4 of the 6 recommendations from the 2021 audit have been fully implemented. The remaining 2 recommendations (relating to fixed asset tagging and vendor master file review) are still in progress. A detailed status update will be presented at the next Finance & Audit Committee meeting.

**4. Reports from Committees**

4.1 **Finance and Audit Committee** (Chair: Cr. Tan Kok Seng)
The Committee met on 5 January 2023. Key matters discussed included the draft budget for FY2023, the quarterly investment report, and the internal audit work plan for 2023. The Committee recommended the budget for Council approval (see Item 7 below).

4.2 **Town Planning Committee** (Chair: Cr. Nadia Rahman)
The Committee met on 8 January 2023. Three development applications were reviewed. The Committee endorsed two applications for approval and deferred one pending further information on traffic impact. The detailed recommendations are circulated separately.

The District Improvement Fund (DIF) annual allocation is 250000 SGD. Record status: current.

4.3 **Community Development Committee** (Chair: Cr. Siti Aminah)
The Committee met on 4 January 2023. The Committee reviewed the calendar of community events for the first half of 2023, including the Riverstone Festival (scheduled for 15-16 April) and the Senior Citizens’ Wellness Week (March). The Committee also discussed the allocation of small grants to grassroots organisations. The recommended grant list is tabled at Item 8.

**5. Chief Executive Officer's Report**

The CEO provided an update on the following operational matters:

- **Flood Mitigation Works:** The first phase of the drainage improvement works at Lorong 3 and Lorong 5 is complete. Phase 2 will commence in March 2023.
- **Digitalisation Programme:** The online service portal for building permits and licence renewals will go live on 1 February 2023. Staff training is underway.
- **Public Engagement on Master Plan:** The public consultation sessions for the draft Master Plan 2023 attracted a total of 1,240 participants across three sessions. Feedback is being collated and will be summarised in a report to the Town Planning Committee in February.

**6. Financial Reports**

6.1 **Operating Budget Performance – Q1 FY2023 (as at 31 December 2022)**
The Council noted the financial report for the period 1 October to 31 December 2022 (first quarter of FY2023). The overall operating expenditure was within budget, with a variance of 2.1% (underspend). The main variance items were:

- Utilities and maintenance – underspent by $45,000 due to lower than expected electricity tariffs.
- Professional fees – overspent by $18,000 due to additional legal costs for the Lorong 3 land acquisition.
The Chairman reported that the position of Council Secretary had been vacant since 1 November 2020, following the retirement of Mrs. Tan Chay Koon. The recruitment exercise was conducted in accordance with the Council’s Staffing Policy and the Public Service Commission guidelines. A total of 24 applications were received, and 6 candidates were shortlisted for interviews. The Selection Panel, comprising the Chairman, the Vice-Chairman, and the CEO, unanimously recommended Ms. Priya Raman for the position.

Ms. Raman holds a Bachelor of Arts (Hons) in Public Policy and Management from the National University of Singapore and has 7 years of experience in public administration, most recently as Assistant Manager (Secretariat) at the Pasir Ris Town Council. Her referees attested to her strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and familiarity with council procedures.

**Resolution M-2021-01:** That the Council approves the appointment of Ms. Priya Raman as Council Secretary with effect from 15 January 2021, and that the terms and conditions of service be in accordance with the Council’s approved staffing framework.

**Motion:** Proposed by Cr. Siti Aminah, seconded by Cr. Rajendran Krishnan.
**Vote:** For 7, Against 0, Abstain 0.
**Carried unanimously.**

Ms. Raman was welcomed by the Chairman and took her seat at the Secretariat table. She will assume full duties with immediate effect, including the preparation of minutes for the next ordinary Council meeting scheduled for 12 February 2021.

The Chairman reported that the term of the current honorary auditors, Messrs. Lim & Koh Associates, will expire on 31 March 2021. The Corporate Services Department had called for quotations from three accounting firms. Two firms submitted proposals. KPMG LLP was the only firm that submitted a proposal within the budgeted fee of $45,000. The other firm, PricewaterhouseCoopers, declined to bid due to a conflict of interest arising from its advisory work for the Council’s digitalisation project.

Ms. Priya Raman appointment date is 2021-01-15. Record status: current.

| Project completion | 30 November 2021 | 15 December 2021 | On track |

3.3 Mr. Ganesan explained that the delay in the earthworks was due to the discovery of an existing underground utility line that was not shown in the available utility plans. The PMO has consulted the relevant utility company and the works have been adjusted accordingly. The revised schedule has been agreed with the contractor, and no additional cost is expected.

3.4 The Committee discussed the delay and asked whether there were any other known discrepancies in the utility plans for the area. Dr. Huda noted that the utility company has been asked to provide updated plans for the entire stretch of Lorong 8, and these are expected by the end of August. The Committee requested that the PMO flag any further discrepancies as soon as they are known.

**1.0 Confirmation of Minutes of Previous Meeting**
1.1 The minutes of the meeting held on 14 November 2023 were confirmed as a correct record. Proposed by Mr. Faisal, seconded by Ms. Tan.

**2.0 Matters Arising**
2.1 **Item 4.2 of previous minutes – Footpath lighting at Clementi Road:** Ms. Tan reported that the contractor has completed the replacement of all faulty LED units. A final inspection was carried out on 8 December 2023 and no defects were found. Item closed.
2.2 **Item 5.1 of previous minutes – Drainage review at Toh Guan estate:** Dr. Huda noted that the PUB has yet to revert on the proposed drainage capacity upgrade. She will chase for a response before the next meeting. Action: Dr. Huda.

**3.0 Green Corridor Phase 2 – Completion and Final Report**
3.1 The Chairperson welcomed all members and noted that this item was the main agenda for the meeting. The Green Corridor Phase 2 project was approved by the Committee in November 2021 with a total budget of S$2.85 million. The project comprises a 3.2 km linear park connecting the existing Green Corridor Phase 1 at Clementi Road to the new residential estate at Toh Guan. Works commenced on 14 March 2022.

3.2 Mr. Ganesan presented the final project report. The project was officially completed on 15 December 2022, and the Contractor's Defects Liability Period (DLP) ended on 14 December 2023. The project team conducted a final walkthrough on 5 December 2023 with representatives from the contractor, the consultant, and NParks. All outstanding defects identified during the DLP have been rectified and verified.

3.3 **Final Budget Statement:**
Mr. Alvin Teo presented the final cost summary:

| Item | Approved Budget (S$) | Actual Expenditure (S$) | Variance (S$) |
|------|----------------------|-------------------------|---------------|
| Construction contract | 2,150,000 | 2,148,750 | (1,250) |
| Professional fees (consultant) | 280,000 | 286,400 | 6,400 |
| Project management & supervision | 120,000 | 118,300 | (1,700) |

| NParks planting & establishment | 100,000 | 98,500 | (1,500) |
| **Total** | **2,850,000** | **2,817,150** | **(32,850)** |

3.4 Mr. Teo explained that the overall project came in under budget by S$32,850. The main savings were from the contingency line, as the earthworks delay did not result in any cost overrun. The slight overrun in professional fees was due to additional site inspection visits required during the extended earthworks period. The Committee noted the final budget statement and approved the closure of the project account.

3.6 **Handover to NParks:**
Ms. Grace Wong confirmed that NParks will take over the maintenance of the Green Corridor Phase 2 from 1 January 2024. The asset register and maintenance manuals have been handed over to NParks. The Committee thanked Ms. Wong and her team for their support.
